title: spectral-noise-correlation-and-eviction-sim-notes
content:
Summary:

This is a working note capturing the "spectral" noisy-tenant pattern we chased on 2026-02-26 -> 2026-02-28 across several dedicated GPU pools. Unlike previous "hot-tenant" or simple KV-cache-thrash patterns, the signature here is intermittent, narrow-band bursts of per-pool latency and packet/PCIe errors that correlate with eviction cascades. The goal of this doc is: 1) summarize evidence, 2) show a simple eviction-simulator we used to sanity-check thresholds, 3) propose temporary mitigations and a lightweight runbook for oncall, and 4) list follow-ups and open questions.

Observed timeline (concise):
- 2026-02-26 03:12 UTC: first alerts from pool-eu-central-2-03: latency p95 increased from ~45ms to ~220ms for ~10m.
- 2026-02-26 03:15 UTC: spike in PCIe AER (Advanced Error Reporting) resets on host h10-03 (found in host exporter).
- 2026-02-26 03:17 UTC: autoscaler initiated eviction of 6 low-priority tenants to alleviate memory pressure; thrash followed and more latency spikes.
- 2026-02-26 03:50 UTC: manual soft-quarantine of one suspected tenant reduced p95 by ~40%.
- 2026-02-27: repeated narrow bursts between 02:30-04:00 UTC with similar PCIe error pattern.

Signals and evidence we correlated:
- Metrics: token_latency_p95_by_pool, kv_cache_miss_rate, tenant_gpu_mem_usage, host_pcie_aer_count, container_restarts, eviction_count.
- Prometheus queries used (examples):
  - token_latency_p95_by_pool{pool="pool-eu-central-2-03"}
  - increase(host_pcie_aer_count_total[5m]) > 0
  - sum by (tenant) (tenant_gpu_mem_mb) / gpu_total_mb_for_host > 0.85  # memory crowding
  - rate(container_restart_count[1m])
- Traces: flamegraphs showed long kernel stalls during the bursts (scheduling wait / driver retransmit delays).
- Host logs: repeated PCIe AER warnings followed by kernel CORRECTABLE_ERROR entries; vendor log indicates transient link errors on PCIe lane 3.

Hypothesis (concise):
A medium-weight tenant is intermittently triggering a device-level condition (PCIe AER) during certain model inference kernels. The device-level retries manifest as short stalls which amplify because several tenants share the same host and the autoscaler eviction policy is too aggressive/fast on downward scale, causing thrashing and cascading evictions rather than quick isolation. The net effect is higher p95 latency, evictions, and sometimes container restarts.

Quick triage checklist (for oncall):
- Paging signal: >3 pool-level p95 latency alerts AND increase(host_pcie_aer_count_total[5m])
- Immediate actions (0-10m):
  1) Identify candidate hosts: prometheus query for hosts with recent AER >0 in last 5m and high p95 pools.
  2) Soft-quarantine suspected tenants (move to quarantine scheduling class or set tenant to low-cpu affinity) — command: opsctl tenant quarantine --tenant-id <id> --pool <pool>
  3) If quarantine not possible: temporarily pin noisy tenants to separate hosts (opsctl tenant migrate --tenant <id> --target-host <host>).
  4) If host-level PCIe errors are rising: place host in maintenance (kube cordon + drain) -> opsctl host quarantine <host> and open vendor ticket.
- Follow-up (10-60m):
  - Check eviction metric trends and confirm no additional churn.
  - If autoscaler kept downscaling/evicting repeatedly, raise the cooldown window (see autoscale config below).

What we simulated: eviction-sensor toy
- Purpose: to test whether our current eviction cooldown + min-free-memory thresholds can cause cascades when a short (1-2 minute) hardware stall reduces available GPU memory briefly (simulated as 10-15% effective memory loss).
- Model: naive event loop where tenants have memory footprints and eviction policy removes low-priority tenants until free memory >= threshold. If evictions occur, some tenants are rescheduled and contending increases.
- Findings: with downscale_cooldown=30s and min_free_mb=0.12*gputotal, a 1-minute stall resulted in 2 sequential evictions within 90s and a subsequent bounce-back reschedule that retriggered the policy. Increasing downscale_cooldown to 5m removed the cascade in the sim.
- Actionable: bump default pool downscale_cooldown from 30s -> 5m for pools with multi-tenant noisy profiles as a temporary mitigation. (PR reference in linked_artifacts).

Autoscaler config notes (current problematic defaults):
- downscale_cooldown: 30s  # too short for transient hardware stalls
- eviction_grace_window: 45s # eviction steps don't wait long enough for short stalls to clear
- min_free_ratio: 0.12
- fallback_model_variant: immediate  # leads to rollbacks that amplify load
Proposal: create a conservative autoscale profile for "mixed-noisy-tenant" pools:
- downscale_cooldown: 5m
- eviction_grace_window: 180s
- min_free_ratio: 0.08 (with conservative overprovision for noisy kernels)
- fallback_model_variant: delayed (30s)

Draft runbook (short, actionable)
- Pager condition: pool_p95_alert && increase(host_pcie_aer_count_total[5m]) > 0 -> page SRE primary (pager) and owner of pool.
- Step 0 (ack): mark incident, add timeline in channel #sre-dedicated-pools, add tag SRE-1729.
- Step 1 (investigate): run prom queries to identify top-3 hosts and top-5 tenants by GPU mem and request rate.
- Step 2 (isolate): soft-quarantine candidate tenant(s); if still noisy, migrate to quarantine hosts.
- Step 3 (stabilize): temporarily increase downscale_cooldown for pool via opsctl autoscale update --pool <pool> --downscale-cooldown 300
- Step 4 (repair): cordon+drain hosts with repeated PCIe errors, open vendor ticket with host serials, attach host logs and vendor-suggested diagnostics.
- Step 5 (post): run postmortem template and attach simulation results, timeline, and a proposed autotune change.

Temporary mitigations we applied (during incident):
- bump downscale_cooldown to 5m on pool-eu-central-2-03 (manual).
- quarantined tenant t-64321 for 2 hours after migration and monitoring -> measured p95 drop ~48%.
- vendor ticket opened (internal ref VEND-563), HBA firmware roll scheduled for host h10-03.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why do PCIe AER bursts map to particular kernels? Is there a model-level pattern (attention tiling, fused kernels)? Need kernel-level profiling on the tenant's model.
- Is there a correlation with PCIe lane assignment / VM placement? Need bin-packing map vs PCIe lanes.
- Could kernel prefetch patterns cause PCIe retrains? Involve HW-accel team to map micro-code behavior.
- Are our default autoscale cooldowns motivated by real workload traces? We have historical anchors but not for this narrow transient pattern. Need longer-tail analysis.

Follow-ups (owners & next steps):
- Suresh: run per-kernel profiler for tenant t-64321 in staging and share trace (due 2026-03-10).
- Marco: create an automated sim harness (python toy) that can run randomized stalls and test autoscale params; add to ops/chaos (due 2026-03-12). PR: linked_artifacts.
- Priya (me): write short runbook snippet in PagerDuty response and update pool autoscale defaults for "noisy-mixed" pools as a staging rollout (due 2026-03-08).
- Evelyn: escalate vendor ticket and coordinate firmware window (due 2026-03-14).

Notes to self / informal:
- This one felt like a halfway hardware + policy bug. The hardware triggers the initial problem but our fast downscale makes it worse by evicting and rescheduling quickly. We should be defensive: treat short hardware stalls as non-actionable for at least 2-3 minutes.
- The simulation is naive but effective as a red-team tool to show how policies amplify transients. Worth standardizing it as part of each pool's postmortem template.

Attachments / logs we referenced (local paths on GCS):
- gs://redwood-logs/pool-eu-central-2-03/2026-02-26/host-h10-03-system.log
- gs://redwood-logs/pool-eu-central-2-03/2026-02-26/prometheus-snap-2026-02-26-0350.prom

Unresolved: should we auto-apply the conservative autoscale profile to all multi-tenant pools? I lean no — do targeted rollout + telemetry to verify.

End of note.
